alternatives_rejected.why: Its own span self-time is unchanged (0.2->0.2ms, 0.99x), and its inbound slowdown appears only on calls from checkoutservice, which is equally slow to five other callees (E3).

proposed_fix.description: Verify whether the node or pod network hosting checkoutservice is the source of the ~200ms delay, and if confirmed, move checkoutservice to a healthy node via a gated, reversible reschedule.
steps: Identify the node and pod(s) running checkoutservice and compare node network metrics (latency, drops, TX/RX errors, retransmits) against other nodes.
Check for network-level latency sources affecting checkoutservice only: tc/netem rules, sidecar/proxy config, NetworkPolicy or CNI changes, and recent deploys or config changes to checkoutservice.
Check conntrack usage on the node (R3) and per-node CPU/memory headroom for networking (R2) as read-only checks.
If the node is shown to be degraded, cordon it (reversible) and, after human approval, restart or reschedule one checkoutservice replica onto a healthy node.
Re-check checkoutservice latency-50/90 and outbound span self-time (E4, E5); if recovered, proceed gradually to remaining replicas, otherwise stop and uncordon.
preconditions: Confirm the slowdown is still ongoing in checkoutservice_latency-50/90 (E5).
Confirm other services on the same node are or are not similarly affected, to distinguish node-wide from pod-specific cause.
Confirm another healthy node has spare capacity and that checkoutservice has more than one replica or acceptable brief disruption.
Obtain on-call approval before cordoning or rescheduling.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node, and if the reschedule did not help, scale or reschedule checkoutservice back to its original placement; revert any config or network policy change made during investigation.
